title: Mock 1: Hamza and Alex, 26 minutes
critique:
What landed
- The bench from the ground up: one snapshot per task, users merged in with duplicate entities renamed (the three Michaels), the harness flag swapping only the provider call, the snapshot reset between runs.
- Honesty about the judge: 'no calibration yet, it is my gut' was the right answer.
- Two metrics in the end: completion (behind calls per task) and completeness against ground truth you hold.

What to fix, in order of cost
1. The design question collapsed. When lost, go to the smallest concrete thing: what the user sees, what they click, what changes next time. The answer was prepared (missFlow).
2. The empty result is the harness inventing a fact: the same provenance gap you criticise in Kitaru. Name it before they do.
3. Metrics took three turns to become concrete. Lead with the two numbers and one worked example.
4. The intro ran about three minutes. Use the 40-second script: what you own, one number, then the bench.
5. Your question to them was generic. Use a prepared one: is replay the wedge, or the product?

Best version of the weakest answer (a better prompt misses every recording)
"I'd make the miss productive. Show the recorded call next to what the new agent sent, old query and new side by side. If they are equivalent, one click accepts it and writes a static alias, so the next replay hits. Deterministic, auditable, no threshold, and every accepted pair is labelled data for automatic matching later.
Then split by effect. A read that misses can fall through to the customer's own environment, marked live on the node. A write that misses fails closed on a fork, never passthrough; at alfred_ every write declares itself as a write.
The limit: this fixes rephrasing, not a different path. For those few sessions, promote the trace into a small queryable world, which is what my bench does. The common case stays free."

On the empty result: "That's a gap. An empty result tells the agent something false. I mark those runs, but I should score them as harness-caused and keep them out of the metric, or return an explicit 'not in snapshot' so the agent cannot mistake it for the truth."
transcript:
Hamza: Tell us what you're working on at alfred_, and what part you own.
Pranav: Founding engineer; making the agent reliable in production: eval infrastructure, memory architecture, orchestration. Working memory: one data model for work items that every source reconciles into. Then the eval bench: a production scanner with cheap rules and a calibrated judge flags failing turns; similar tasks across users are collected, their tool calls unioned and their fetched data put into one SQLite snapshot per task, with entities deduplicated; the real agent runs with a harness flag that swaps provider calls for the snapshot; the snapshot resets between runs.

Alex: If the agent calls a tool not in the snapshot, what does pass through mean? Does it hit Gmail? How would you know?
Pranav: It never leaves the machine. The agent gets an empty result back; the call is marked so the snapshot can be enriched.

Alex/Hamza: An empty result is a plausible answer. The agent concludes there are no meeting notes. How does scoring tell a bad call from a good call on a lie the harness told?
Pranav: With rich enough aggregation it rarely happens; the north star is turns or tool calls per completed task; out-of-union calls are flagged.

Hamza: An agent that stops early on the empty set looks more efficient. What makes a run count as done, concretely?
Pranav: Completion is the task done; failed runs are a separate class.

Alex: Four action items, the agent makes three. Pass or fail, and what decides?
Pranav: Pass on completion. Ground truth per instance is known, so completeness is a second, orthogonal score; judged now with Claude Code rather than an LLM judge.

Alex: How do you know the judge didn't move when the pass rate moves?
Pranav: No calibration yet; the harness is local and judged on my gut. Ground truth stays fixed; the bench reruns on tool, agent or subtask changes, and the reconciler appends new production cases.

Hamza: A customer imports Langfuse traces, improves the prompt, the CRM query changes, half the cohort misses and dies. What do we build?
Pranav: A read-tool policy that executes against the user's environment; simulated users; not sure.
Alex: Tomorrow morning the customer sees half the runs died. What should that screen show?
Pranav: The recorded call against what the agent did; then last-turn replay, stateful world, simulated user; not sure.
Hamza: They say the two searches are the same. What button, and what changes for the next replay?
Pranav: Not sure; a bit lost.

Hamza: Questions for us?
Pranav: What do you need from a product engineer specifically?
